attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'In which cases' takes over the earlier antecedent (enough customers have second thoughts, so none of the three hits its projections). 'Will eventually fall' is firm wording with no deadline. The general disclaimer later in the post does not hedge this sentence.

contract.note: Fair. The companies, threshold, projections and reference price are not specified, and the contract names these as evaluator choices. It rightly says that no decline so far cannot count as failure, given 'eventually'.

evidence.note: SpaceX traded below its IPO price by July 2026. That is one candidate stock, the antecedent is not established, and it is not a decline after a projection failure.
Company disclosure: Anthropic's S-1 was not yet effective on Oct 26, so there is no trading history. It cannot show the outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. Nothing in the packet shows the antecedent happened: no customer pullback reaching 'enough', and no failure by all three companies to meet their projections. At least one candidate had not listed by the cutoff. Under the policy an unknown antecedent is not scored, and a period with no decline is not failure. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus states this in his own voice, summarising reported facts. He endorses it.

semantics.note: The proposition matches both parts: the annual token budget was used up within a few months, and spending is not paying off as hoped.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. Claude Code is paid for by token use, so its budget reasonably counts as the AI 'token' budget, and the COO's remarks fit 'not working out as hoped'.

evidence.note: The COO said higher token use did not produce matching gains in useful features. His mild hedge does not change that.
Reports that the CTO said in April that Uber had already used up its full-year 2026 Claude Code budget.
Independent report that the whole planned 2026 AI coding budget was used up in four months, which fits 'a few months'.

reviews.rationale: Two reputable outlets report the CTO saying Uber used up its full-year 2026 AI coding budget, which is token-priced, within four months. The COO said publicly that the gains do not match the rising AI costs. Both parts of the observation hold on the plain reading, and the packet contains no counterevidence.

attribution.note: Marcus gives the cause in his own voice before embedding the Techmeme/Reuters post.

semantics.note: The claim says the shutdown happened and that Starbucks ended the tool because it realised the tool could not be trusted. The causal part is the core of the claim.

contract.note: The two-part test is fair. To contradict, the contract needs evidence of reasons unrelated to accuracy. The company's 'standardize' statement does not clearly meet that bar, so the result depends on how the stated reason is read.

evidence.note: Reuters confirms the tool was retired in the week of May 18 and had documented miscounts. This supports the shutdown and the record of unreliability, but Reuters does not say the errors caused the shutdown.
An employee comment shared by the company says 'execution was proving difficult'. It is weak and selective, and does not show why Starbucks made the decision.
Company disclosure giving standardisation as the reason. That differs from the cause Marcus states, but it is self-reported and does not show the decision was unrelated to accuracy.

reviews.rationale: The shutdown is confirmed, and so is the tool's record of miscounting. The stated cause, that Starbucks ended it because it could not be trusted, is neither confirmed nor ruled out. Reuters only places the errors next to the shutdown, and the company gives a different reason in a self-serving statement. The causal claim at the centre is not settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: This is a firm conditional ('will ever'). Adding 'about AI' is a small gloss, but the context supports it. The antecedent is kept, and there is no deadline.

contract.note: Fair. It refuses to define 'enough' after the fact, requires the projections that existed at the time of the post, and does not treat interim weakness as resolving the claim. The unnamed companies and metrics leave the result to interpretation.

evidence.note: Some enterprise customers have cut spending or switched supplier. That does not establish that 'enough' customers pulled back, and it says nothing about projection outcomes.
Company filing showing customer growth. It is a self-disclosure and does not address whether the long-term projections were met.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish the antecedent, a large enough customer pullback, and it does not identify the three companies' original long-term projections or any outcome against them. With no deadline and the condition unknown, the forecast cannot be scored from this evidence.
